title: Structural Plumbing Mixed with Environment Configuration
damaged_code:
```yaml
# application_wiring_and_secrets.yaml
database_connection:
  driver_name: "org.postgresql.Driver" # Changing this breaks class-loading invariants
  pool_size: 15
  username: "prod_user"
  password: "highly_secret_password" # Operators must edit this file live to rotate keys
```
pattern: Mixing structural system wiring metadata (like dependency injection beans or class bindings) with mutable environment configuration values (like passwords and hostnames) in a single file.
why_bad: Forces operators to edit giant XML/YAML files containing complex application internals just to update an environmental variable (like a database password). A typo in non-variable sections turns structural plumbing into active production landmines, causing opaque runtime crashes.
detection: Configuration schemas containing class names, serialization rules, or object graphs alongside secret credentials or network hostnames.
counterexample:
```yaml
# application_secrets.yaml - isolated and strictly access-controlled
database_password: "highly_secret_password"
```
fix: Isolate production properties from basic plumbing definitions; store secret parameters and hostnames in dedicated properties files or environments separate from dependency injections.
source: [Pragmatic Programmers] Michael T. Nygard - *Release It!_ Design and Deploy Production-Ready Software* (2007, Pragmatic Bookshelf).pdf, Section 14.2.
